raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Overview This PR adds online integer quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 checkpoints on Ascend NPU. It supports load-time weight conversion and dynamic activation quantization for SRT dense linear and MoE layers, plus the native diffusion W8A8 path. The supported SRT modes are: - `w8a8_int`: W8A8 for supported dense projections and MoE experts. - `w4a4_int`: mixed Qwen3-MoE mode, using W8A8 for dense projections and W4A4 for MoE `w13`/`w2` experts. Dense-only architectures are rejected because dense W4A4 has not met the accuracy requirement. This is separate from offline ModelSlim or other pre-quantized checkpoint formats. ## Key Changes ### SRT Ascend online quantization - Selects online W8A8 for unquantized NPU `q/k/v/qkv/o`, `gate/up/gate_up`, and `down` projections. Existing checkpoint-quantized and non-NPU paths are unchanged. - Converts dense and MoE source weights as soon as their logical shards are completely loaded, instead of retaining a full-model FP16/BF16 copy until post-load processing. - Preserves shard-aware QKV, merged-column, row-parallel, TP, and EP loading behavior. - Uses `npu_dynamic_quant` for weight and activation quantization, then `npu_quant_matmul` or NPU grouped matmul with backend-required weight and scale layouts. - Validates dense and MoE completion-tracked loader state before post-load use, including reload handling. - Detects Ascend through the runtime torch-NPU path so dense online quantization also works when no out-of-tree `SRTPlatform` plugin is active. ### W4A4 policy - Keeps known-good Qwen3-MoE W4A4 expert layouts for `w13` and W8A8 for `w2`. - Keeps dense projections on W8A8 in mixed mode. - Rejects `--online-quantization w4a4_int` for unsupported dense architectures during NPU argument resolution. ### Diffusion - Adds the native Ascend `w8a8_int` transformer quantization method for unquantized diffusion components. - Keeps diffusion component quantization routed through `--transformer-quantization` / component quantization settings rather than the SRT LLM flag. ### Tests and documentation - Adds focused NPU unit coverage for mode selection, dense projection policy, source dtypes, scale layouts, loader completion states, reload behavior, and platform detection. - Documents the SRT and diffusion online quantization interfaces. ## Usage ### Qwen3-32B W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w8a8_int ``` ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w4a4_int ``` ### MiniMax-H3 diffusion W8A8 ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ sglang serve \ --model-path /home/weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 8 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --transformer-quantization w8a8_int \ --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload ``` ## Validation ### Qwen3-32B dense path bf16: w8a8: ### MiniMax-H3 BF16: W8A8: ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 BF16: W8A8: Mixed W4A4/W8A8: ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide available accuracy and memory results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #37291946215](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37291946215) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #37291945835](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37291945835) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #37291946084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37291946084)

detail.body: ## Overview This PR adds online integer quantization for unquantized FP16/BF16 checkpoints on Ascend NPU. It supports load-time weight conversion and dynamic activation quantization for SRT dense linear and MoE layers, plus the native diffusion W8A8 path. The supported SRT modes are: - `w8a8_int`: W8A8 for supported dense projections and MoE experts. - `w4a4_int`: mixed Qwen3-MoE mode, using W8A8 for dense projections and W4A4 for MoE `w13`/`w2` experts. Dense-only architectures are rejected because dense W4A4 has not met the accuracy requirement. This is separate from offline ModelSlim or other pre-quantized checkpoint formats. ## Key Changes ### SRT Ascend online quantization - Selects online W8A8 for unquantized NPU `q/k/v/qkv/o`, `gate/up/gate_up`, and `down` projections. Existing checkpoint-quantized and non-NPU paths are unchanged. - Converts dense and MoE source weights as soon as their logical shards are completely loaded, instead of retaining a full-model FP16/BF16 copy until post-load processing. - Preserves shard-aware QKV, merged-column, row-parallel, TP, and EP loading behavior. - Uses `npu_dynamic_quant` for weight and activation quantization, then `npu_quant_matmul` or NPU grouped matmul with backend-required weight and scale layouts. - Validates dense and MoE completion-tracked loader state before post-load use, including reload handling. - Detects Ascend through the runtime torch-NPU path so dense online quantization also works when no out-of-tree `SRTPlatform` plugin is active. ### W4A4 policy - Keeps known-good Qwen3-MoE W4A4 expert layouts for `w13` and W8A8 for `w2`. - Keeps dense projections on W8A8 in mixed mode. - Rejects `--online-quantization w4a4_int` for unsupported dense architectures during NPU argument resolution. ### Diffusion - Adds the native Ascend `w8a8_int` transformer quantization method for unquantized diffusion components. - Keeps diffusion component quantization routed through `--transformer-quantization` / component quantization settings rather than the SRT LLM flag. ### Tests and documentation - Adds focused NPU unit coverage for mode selection, dense projection policy, source dtypes, scale layouts, loader completion states, reload behavior, and platform detection. - Documents the SRT and diffusion online quantization interfaces. ## Usage ### Qwen3-32B W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w8a8_int ``` ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --device npu \ --attention-backend ascend \ --online-quantization w4a4_int ``` ### MiniMax-H3 diffusion W8A8 ```bash SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \ sglang serve \ --model-path /home/weights/MiniMax-H3/ \ --model-type diffusion \ --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 8 \ --tp-size 2 \ --sp-degree 4 \ --attention-backend laser_attn \ --transformer-quantization w8a8_int \ --component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload ``` ## Validation ### Qwen3-32B dense path bf16: w8a8: ### MiniMax-H3 BF16: W8A8: ### Qwen3-30B-A3B mixed W4A4/W8A8 BF16: W8A8: Mixed W4A4/W8A8: ## Checklist - +
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        input_size_per_partition: int,
+        output_partition_sizes: list[int],
+        input_size: int,
+        output_size: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs,

+                sum(output_partition_sizes),
+                input_size_per_partition,
+                dtype=params_dtype,
+            ),

+            output_dim=0,
+            weight_loader=extra_weight_attrs.get("weight_loader"),

+        )
